page: Amazon Web Services m4.2xlarge is a general-purpose instance powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2686 v4 processor. Utilizing the x86_64 architecture, this instance provides 8 vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It features 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. The CPU operates at a clock speed of 2.4 GHz and includes a 45 MB L3 cache. This instance runs on the Xen hypervisor, lacks local storage, and does not include any GPU accelerators. Network connectivity is limited to a baseline bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates that the m4.2xlarge exhibits moderate multi-core and memory capabilities alongside weaker single-core performance. Multi-core CPU performance via stress-ng and PassMark CPU scores fall within the average range, as does the static web serving throughput of 6.25 GB/sec. However, single-core metrics, including Geekbench single-core and single-threaded gzip compression, are positioned in the bottom 25%. Memory bandwidth remains average, with read-only large block speeds at 46.46 GB/sec and write speeds at 34.84 GB/sec. Large-model LLM inference and database operations, such as Redis SET, score in the lower percentiles, reflecting the older CPU architecture.

The qualitative cost profile of the m4.2xlarge reflects its status as an older-generation general-purpose resource. While it offers a stable allocation of dedicated vCPUs and balanced memory density, the lack of local NVMe storage and the modest 1 Gbps baseline network bandwidth represent significant tradeoffs for modern, I/O-heavy workloads. This instance is suited for legacy general-purpose applications, basic web serving, and moderate multi-threaded processing tasks that do not require high single-core throughput or fast local disk access.
